## A publication-first website starter

<p class="lede">This sample homepage shows how the UNICEF Quarto design variant can shape a light, readable, and strongly branded website for reports, storytelling, guidance, and advocacy content.</p>

## What This Demo Includes

<div class="unicef-card-grid">
  <div class="unicef-card">
    <h3>Publication rhythm</h3>
    <p>Large, calm headings, generous line spacing, and narrow reading measures suited to reports, briefs, and story pages.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="unicef-card">
    <h3>Quarto navigation</h3>
    <p>A top navbar, docked sidebar, search, reader mode, back-to-top navigation, and page navigation across content.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="unicef-card">
    <h3>Structured content</h3>
    <p>Callouts, tables, code blocks, and footer areas styled to feel like part of the same UNICEF editorial system.</p>
  </div>
</div>

## Design Principles

- Keep the site light-first and content-led.
- Use UNICEF Blue as the strongest brand signal, not as decoration on every element.
- Favor readability over novelty.
- Let photography lead major landing and campaign moments, while analytical pages stay quieter.
- Preserve a credible, global-public-interest tone.
